Christine Dunnett's inmate has tumbled down the handicap and would be a threat to all if able to dictate terms. The lightly-raced Zaramara is also noted.

selections.comment: The impeccably bred DAVY CROCKETT can make a winning debut over hurdles. A facile scorer on his introduction in a bumper at Punchestown last month, the Willie Mullins-trained gelding looks an exciting prospect. Almost certainly destined for greater things in time, the once-raced gelding can make it two from two. Former smart Flat handicapper Ephesus looks his biggest danger. Rated 89 on the level, the Denis Hogan-trained gelding was deemed good enough to contest a Grade 1 race last time. Although out of contention when unseating late on, he will find this easier. Mick Collins is also capable of making his presence felt for Noel Meade.

selections.comment: Lightly raced four-year-old RAKKI catches the eye on stable debut for Willie Mullins. Although yet to get his head in front, the Sea The Stars gelding could prove to be well treated relative to his mark on the Flat. While his lack of handicap experience is an obvious worry in a field of this size, he might be worth taking a chance on. Runner-up in the corresponding race last year, Clonbury Bridge is sure to have been laid out for a repeat bid. A winner over fences at Fairyhouse in January, the nine-year-old is able to compete from a 7lb lower mark back over hurdles. Wajaaha is another to consider.

selections.comment: With the benefit of previous experience and a favourable low draw, it is difficult to look past CONSTITUTION RIVER. The Aidan O'Brien-trained colt looks a winner without a penalty, having only lost out by a short-head on his racecourse debut at Newmarket earlier this month. Granted normal improvement, the son of Wootton Bassett should prove very hard to beat. Given the record of Dermot Weld in this race over the years, his newcomer Masaban deserves maximum respect. A half-brother to a black-type filly, the son of Siyouni will have had this as a target for some time. Spangled Sands could also be involved for his in-form stable.

Graded bumper and hurdle winner Familiar Dreams and the Joseph O'Brien-trained Comfort Zone are others to consider.

selections.comment: AVIATRICE shaped well on her seasonal return at Limerick before finding trouble in running at Leopardstown next time. David Marnane's filly has few miles on the clock and still looks feasibly handicapped, while the plumb draw in stall one will do her chances no harm either. Gowran scorer Highbury See See is also berthed well and does not look overburdened by a subsequent 9lb rise, especially with Sam Coen removing a handy 7lb in the plate. Oiche Rua should not be overlooked either.

selections.comment: DESMOND CASTLE has been a work in progress for some time and can now make the breakthrough. He ducked sharply left and unseated rider coming out of stalls last September and, while he has been finding his feet since, he was hampered at Limerick earlier this month before finishing his race in eye-catching fashion. Connections are likely to have had this race in mind and he remains unexposed over this distance. His trainer has a very strong hand with Bear Creek, although he is 10lb higher than when scoring at Down Royal. Starford is also noted.

Purchased for 38,000 euros as a three-year-old, his dam is related to Flat winners and any market confidence would only enhance his claims. Maskarvel has proven form and nice ability having contested a useful Killarney bumper. I'm A Rocket Man is closely matched with Maskarvel on Punchestown form, while debutant Gomez Addams is also of interest.

SKI ANGEL won her penultimate start and looks the best chance of Mike Smith's two, he has won 2 of the last 5 runnings of this race (including with this horse in 2023) and looks primed for another big run. Winner of the race last year Zuffolo shouldn't be too far behind, he won from a 1lb higher mark last year and was unlucky last time out. Moyola can make up the places, a revival is needed but is down to a very tempting mark now.

They could both find this distance more suitable and are open to improvement on their second handicap starts.

But he might have to settle with filling the places in this.

And Little Saver can fill the places on his second start since the gelding operation.

selections.comment: DAVY CROCKETT's half brother took this a few years ago before winning a Grade 1 the following spring and connections will be hoping he can follow in those footsteps. He was an impressive winner of his sole start in bumpers and should be capable of following up on his hurdles bow on favourable good ground. Useful flat performer Ephesus looks the biggest threat after some solid efforts at higher levels despite some poor rides. The return to a sound surface could bring some improvement and he can chase the selection home ahead of A Snow White Park who was a fortunate winner on debut but should have more to offer.

selections.comment: An open race where last year's winner Son Of Hypnos is strongly respected off 6lb higher this time. He has caught the eye on a couple of recent starts finishing off his races well under tender handling. All of his best form has come under positive handling so having dropped back to a suitable mark it would be no surprise to see him resuming those tactics. However he could be vulnerable to an unexposed rival and RAKKI certainly fits the bill starting out for top connections. When last seen in the UK he finished a place behind a useful rival who placed in the Fred Winter in the spring and he looks on a good mark on that form. His flat form suggests this better ground will suit so he should make a winning stable debut. Of those at bigger prices Space Warrior makes minor appeal for a yard no stranger to a winner here. Things haven't gone to plan of late but he is well treated on his winning debut form and could revive back on a sound surface.

selections.comment: This could be fought out by the dual purpose yards. Too Bossy For Us looks the pick of the Mullins stable on jockey bookings and he is open to improvement on just his second flat start for the yard. It will also be just his second run over 2m and he is open to improvement judged on his solid efforts at the top level in juvenile hurdles in the spring. It is Graded hurdle and bumper winner FAMILIAR DREAMS who is marginally preferred though racing off what looks a potentially lenient opening mark. She travelled strongly when beating Happy Jacky at a tight track on her last flat run and should progress now upped in distance. Jospeh O'Brien also holds a strong hand with Comfort Zone looking his main hope judged on his Royal Ascot placing. However it is stablemate Dawn Rising who could fare better at generous odds. The veteran has been out of form this term but proved he retained his ability with a Group win in the autumn and he's proven himself effective on big weights in handicaps before.

She is another with an AW victory to her name who looks ahead of her current mark.
